items.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998
items.q: So he called me in about an Eileen Rogers... Don Cherry was doing two songs... So what he’s telling me is, “I’ve got a conductor hired, Norm Layton is going to be conducting” for Don Cherry... So this was the first time. Up to now in my career... ctx.x: Well you must have had an arrangement like with Columbia, did you get a percentage of the recording? Were you on contract?

Oh I started out like all the rest of the artists. The first break I got was through Mitch Miller. I met Mitch when I was writing for Harry James’ band, and he would come out to the west coast, and sit in the booth and oversee the sessions. And when I first went back to New York, this is let’s say five or six years later, after I’d been doing arranging for Harry James, I went back — I’d been on the west coast for a while and I decided gee I used to do, I was doing well, but I thought I could be doing better. I said, “you know if you need any arranging done, I’m here, available now,” and he says, “fine, I’ll keep you in mind“ the old line you know — don’t call us we’ll call you.
